compensating.why: hop 1 falls back to toString() instead of name()
hop 3 passes an empty explicit name through
hop 2 treats every runtime exception as no explicit name

ownership_reason: Only the gold locates the field of an enumeration constant and reads its @JsonProperty annotation; hops 1-4 receive the constant and the gold's result only (hop 1 falls back to name(), hop 2 treats a SecurityException as no explicit name, hop 3 treats an empty name as none, hop 4 passes the value through), so no caller can hand the gold another class or pre-filter the constant. The gold's javadoc promises the name that @JsonProperty on the constant's field gives it; for a constant with a body (an instance of an anonymous subclass of its enumeration type) the variant searches the subclass, finds no field and returns null although the field carries @JsonProperty("b"). The convention is pinned outside the gold: ClassUtil.findEnumType(Enum) and findEnumType(Class) take the superclass of a constant's class when it is not Enum ('enums with body are sub-classes of the formal type'), used in production by EnumValues.constructFromName / constructFromToString and ClassNameIdResolver; TestClassUtil::testFindEnumType passes, and TestEnumSerialization::testSubclassedEnums and TestEnumDeserialization::testSubclassedEnums pass through the chain with bodied constants.
